source.title: Exact solutions of a deep linear network
source.authors: Liu Ziyin; Botao Li; Xiangmin Meng

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and demonstrates outcomes for training deep linear networks and nonlinear networks, bearing on training difficulty and depth, but does not use the benchmark classification recipes in the versions.
record.gate_note: Reports theoretical results for deep linear networks with weight decay and stochastic neurons, plus experiments on synthetic tasks and CIFAR-10. CIFAR-10 training loss/accuracy details appear only as a figure reference; the text describes the ResNet18 performance dropping to a trivial-model level. The paper does not test most claim versions' specific recipes.
record.test_reason: The study establishes weight-decay-dependent landscape properties and demonstrates collapse, but does not test the specific behaviors and comparisons in V1–V6. Local-minimum existence does not measure depth-dependent training classification error or convergence frequency. Its initialization argument does not compare initialization schemes or measure signal and gradient propagation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but the origin is not always a bad minimum: it is always a strict local minimum under the stated depth and positive-regularization assumptions, and is bad when a better nontrivial solution exists. The authors derive global-minimum forms for stochastic deep linear networks, argue that weight decay complicates their landscape and can undermine standard initialization, and offer limited nonlinear demonstrations.
record.recipe_differences: The main analysis is theoretical for deep linear networks with weight decay and stochastic neurons, using squared error; empirical demonstrations include synthetic regression and a standard-procedure CIFAR10 ResNet18. It does not reproduce the claim's gradient-training classification benchmark recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical bad-minimum result depends on depth D ≥ 2 and positive weight decay; the synthetic nonlinear models are described as stuck for sufficiently small signal ||E[xy]|| under Kaiming initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: With positive weight decay and at least two hidden layers, the origin is a strict local minimum of the linear-network objective; it is nonglobal when a better nontrivial solution exists. With one hidden layer, the origin is a saddle or global minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay can create a spurious zero-output minimum in deep linear networks, with a qualitative change between one and two hidden layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Kaiming-initialized, two-hidden-layer ReLU and tanh networks remain at the trivial solution on sufficiently weak-signal synthetic regression tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard initialization can fail to escape a trivial solution on weak-signal regression tasks in the studied regularized setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports ResNet18 performance on CIFAR-10 falling to a trivial-model level as weight decay increases, whereas the linear regressor does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections do not universally prevent performance collapse under strong weight decay.

record.problems: Theoretical claims assume linear networks with squared loss, weight decay, and stochastic neurons; the authors caution that relevance to nonlinear models is conditional. Nonlinear demonstrations are limited, figure-based, and report no error bars; the CIFAR10 comparison gives no numeric training classification error. Experiment code is reported as not provided.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, training duration, and regularization.
Gradient-descent convergence to spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and its reduction through extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, prevention through identity shortcuts, and the special initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
Comparative training speed and trainable depth under activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient preservation, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian initialization.
Loss recovery, divergence, and sharpness dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's broader claims about optimization difficulty do not establish the narrower versions supplied here. The supplied text does not expose Figure 1's numerical axes or distinguish training from test performance.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/100 training classification error sweep over model sizes, random/corrupted labels, optimizers, or training durations.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or student-width sweep.

Tests whether depth and weight decay can create a bad local minimum in deep linear networks and reports a CIFAR-10 ResNet18 collapse illustration. Does not compare plain batch-normalized and shortcut networks, or test special initialization and normalization-free residual recipes.
No comparison of initialization schemes for speed or trainable depth; Kaiming initialization is only discussed and used in the synthetic experiment.
No learning-rate sweep around a stability threshold or sharpness measurement.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup experiment.

rows.subject: deep linear net (D ≥ 2)
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed the zero-parameter solution's local-minimum status with positive weight decay.
rows.measure: Whether the all-zero parameter setting is a local minimum
rows.value: Always a local minimum with a diagonal positive-definite Hessian γI.
rows.note: This theoretical result concerns local-minimum status, not measured training classification error.
rows.check: Proposition 2 establishes a strict local minimum in regularized linear networks, not V3's training-error comparison between plain and residual convolutional networks. The origin is not necessarily nonglobal; that requires additional conditions. Appendix B.7 gives Hessian entries 2γu and 2γw for the corresponding parameter blocks, rather than a universal γI.

rows.subject: depth-1 linear net (D = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the zero solution's local-minimum status with deeper networks.
rows.measure: Whether the zero solution is a bad local minimum
rows.value: The point b = 0 is either a saddle or the global minimum; it is not a bad minimum.
rows.note: Depth-1 is a theoretical comparison, not a CIFAR classification result.
rows.check: The depth-1 landscape result does not measure V3's behavior. Its lack of a bad minimum at zero is not a reversal of V3. Here D counts hidden layers.

rows.subject: D = 2 neural networks with ReLU and Tanh
rows.size_stated: hidden width 32 for both hidden layers
rows.stage_stated: trained from Kaiming initialization with SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained synthetic regression networks for 10^4 iterations across tasks with varying signal strength.

conditions.value: 1000 points, x ∼ N(0, I5), linear target y = v ⋅ x

rows.baseline: Optimized linear regressor is better than the trivial solution when ||E[xy]|| > 0.
rows.value: For sufficiently small ||E[xy]||, the nonlinear models are stuck at the origin; figure only for individual values.
rows.uncertainty: No error bars; fluctuations described as visually negligible in checklist.
rows.locator: Figure 3; Section 5, “Insufficiency of the existing initialization schemes”; Appendix A
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the outcome, but supplies no precise per-condition values. This is a synthetic regression demonstration, not benchmark classification error.
rows.check: Weak-signal synthetic regression failure under one initialization measures neither V3's convolutional depth comparison nor V4's comparative training speed or trainable depth. Appendix A specifies gradient descent, whereas Section 5 says SGD; the record should preserve this discrepancy. The experimental weight-decay strength is not specified in the supplied details.

rows.subject: ResNet18 on CIFAR10

conditions.value: standard procedure; standard augmentations such as random crop

rows.measure: Performance relative to a trivial model
rows.baseline: A linear regressor never drops to the performance of a trivial model.
rows.value: Performance drops to the level of a trivial model, like a deep linear net with similar depth.
rows.locator: Figure 1 caption; Section 5, “Landscape of multi-layer neural networks”; Appendix A
rows.note: The text describes the CIFAR10 ResNet18 comparison, but does not report a numeric training-error value. The claim's classification-error measure cannot be determined from this description.
rows.check: The qualitative performance collapse does not identify training classification error, so it cannot establish V1's outcome. There is no plain-versus-residual depth comparison for V3. Figure 1 describes increasing weight decay, which the row omits. Parameter count should read approximately 10^7.
